scope: bibcheck/journal_key.xls, every row with a target (format_journal_name aliases)
method: Each of the 450 rows with a target (448 distinct sources after the pandas to_dict duplicate collapse; 648 further rows have no target and never apply) was classified as (a) same journal, (b) different_journal, (c) misspelled_target, using NLM Catalog E-utilities (nlmcatalog esearch/esummary, <=1 req/s), Crossref /journals and /works, Open Library, and the cdl.bib entries that use each name. A dictionary scan of every target word found the misspellings.
fix_method: bibcheck/journal_key_overrides.json, applied by helpers.load_key_overrides() to journal_key only. The .xls is legacy BIFF (Excel 2004-era); only xlrd (read-only) is installed, and rewriting it would need a new unmaintained writer (xlwt), would rewrite the whole binary and give an unreviewable diff. The JSON carries the evidence, and the loader raises if the spreadsheet's target no longer equals the recorded old_target.

regression_check.method: format_journal_name over every distinct journal and booktitle value in `git show HEAD:cdl.bib`, before vs after
regression_check.note: No HEAD value changes: cdl.bib already stores formatted names, so no wrong-row source string survives in it. The corrupted values (e.g. 'Physiological Review') are not alias sources and format to themselves both before and after; they need source-verified edits to cdl.bib, listed below.
